chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Wahb, from Abi Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Jizya, so he said: 'Verily, Allah the Exalted has made the Jizya specific to the polytheists of the Arabs.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the Jizya tax specifically restricted to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the divine prohibition of Jizya specifically targets the polytheists of the Arabs (Mushrik al-Arab), distinguishing them from the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) who are explicitly permitted to pay it. This hadith highlights the nuanced application of Islamic fiscal law, where the general permission for Jizya is limited by this specific exclusion, reflecting the historical context of the Arab polytheists' unique status prior to and during the early Islamic conquests.
